source.solution: Without loss of generality, let \(a_{1} \leq a_{2} \leq \cdots \leq a_{2023}\). Then, note that \(a_{k+1}-a_{k}=\sum_{i=1}^{2023}\left|a_{k+1}-a_{i}\right|-\left|a_{k}-a_{i}\right|=k(a_{k+1}-a_{k})-(2023-k)(a_{k+1}-a_{k})=(2k-2023)(a_{k+1}-a_{k})\). Thus, \(a_{k+1}=a_{k}\) unless \(k=1012\), so \(a_{1}=a_{2}=\cdots=a_{1012}\) and \(a_{1013}=\cdots=a_{2023}\), and we can check that that they must be in a ratio of \(1011:1012\). Thus, \(a_{1}, \ldots, a_{2023}\) must consist of 1012 copies of \(1011c\), and 1011 copies of \(1012c\) for some \(c\), so for everything to be a positive integer, we need \(c \geq 1\). This gives us the final answer of \(1011 \cdot 1012+1012 \cdot 1011=2046264\).
